assertion_analysis.fails_if: a ready dispatch is refused by the waiting claim
dispatch returns a phase other than starting
dispatch changes the waiting pointer phase, but it does not distinguish a phase-specific regression because both sides use the phase parameter
the waiting claim makes scope widening raise
the working claim no longer refuses dispatch
the refusal reports another error than scope-conflict
the queued request is not initially awaiting-upstream
the waiting request launches despite the working holder
the waiting request does not become queued after its upstream declaration
no failure is recorded, though any unrelated failure also satisfies it

findings.text: blocking: The new waiting-phase disposition duplicates the owner at reckon/crew/node.py:1527, so dispatch treats awaiting-upstream and held claims as nonbinding while the production registry at reckon/crew/runs.py:1125 still reports them binding; move the shared phase rule into the owner before landing.

findings.disposition_reason: Independent dispatch and mutation assertions already guard the behavior.
findings.text: non-blocking: This assertion compares the stored phase with the same phase supplied to the fixture, so changing that supplied phase moves both sides together and it cannot prove the phase-specific refusal was fixed; exempted because lines 26-27 and the recorded negative control independently guard that behavior.

non-blocking: A truthy failure can come from an unrelated admission error, so the test does not identify the working holder as the reason the waiter stayed queued; folded into the required claim-disposition repair for this node.
